clusters.name: Secondary school and his stepfather's place, 1987–1988
clusters.reason: Around the time Jonah entered secondary school, his relationship with his stepfather Desmond shifted to distance while his bond with his father Russell remained warm. His stepmother left Desmond over a baby question, and Jonah made the city chess squad but felt out of his depth, raising his anxiety. These shifts in his key relationships and his own anxiety piled up as he navigated a new school and household.

clusters.name: First year away and his grandfather's death, 1989–1992
clusters.reason: Jonah's grandfather Gordon died in June 1991 after Jonah had left home for the conservatory that September 1991. Within weeks of arriving he hurt his wrist and stopped playing, his anxiety and functioning collapsed, he fought with his closest friend Rafe who moved out, and he sank into isolation and symptoms. His father Clifford returned to the family around 1989 after years away. Across this stretch Jonah's functioning fell, his anxiety rose, and he developed symptoms of substance use and depression. His mother filled in his college forms as he underfunctioned, and his grandmother's health shifted. By early 1992 he was lost and low with no footing.

clusters.name: Performance peak and split with Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Jonah bonded with Joelle in early 1998 and began performing at his best, winning competitions. By 1999 insomnia began interfering with his playing though he still functioned at his height. He and Joelle separated within the year and he started therapy with Victor Halloran, telling him about his family's gambling history and beginning to see it as part of a larger pattern. His anxiety rose around the split while his performance functioning peaked, then fell.

clusters.name: Burnout and the long slump, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around 2001–2002 Jonah's performing fell apart. He had a disastrous audition in his home town and ran out of steam for performance while his anxiety rose and functioning fell. His grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer around this time. He moved away from Thornbury to Gull Harbour in late 2002 to distance from family and friends, met Marisol and moved to Fenwick with her in 2003, then split from her within months. He sank into deep depression that winter, unable to move from the sofa. He returned to Thornbury and avoided his family, relying on friends instead. His functioning gradually rose again only after returning to therapy with Victor Halloran in early 2004. His grandmother died in February 2004 after spending her final months in his mother and stepfather's home. His anxiety remained high and his contact with his grandmother stayed distant.

clusters.name: Nursing school and cutoff from his mother, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Jonah's grandmother Lorna died in January 2008 and his grandfather Clifford died around the same time. That summer he was too drained for conversation with his mother at Alder Creek and grew anxious when she pressed him to visit, leading to conflict when she came anyway. He stopped speaking to his mother when he left for nursing school in September 2008, a cutoff that held for roughly a year as he could not afford to call. His aunt Imogen had a stroke with months of rehabilitation around 2009. His functioning was low through the early nursing programme but began to recover as he gained footing in the work.

clusters.name: Marriage and his partner's enmeshment, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Jonah married Wren in March 2017 and contact with his mother eased off slightly. By late 2019 his partner's cousin Alice had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis and his partner was swamped with events. Wren talks with her father and brother all day in a fusion, nothing happens to one without the others hearing. When she was swamped by a street party, fundraiser and her mother's retirement at the lake, Jonah overfunctioned laying out plans to settle her. At the lake weekend Jonah's sleep collapsed—he was awake from the small hours and felt he did not belong. His anxiety rose and he distanced from the group. His partner became anxious watching his state. His job had steadied and paid well but he constantly felt he ought to drive his projects forward, a driving anxiety he has carried since the conservatory days.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
